title.narrative: Livelihoods Support to Flood Affected Victims in Idah, Kogi State

description.narrative: Kogi State in North Central Nigeria is one of the states that experiences regular flooding due to its location at the convegence of the Niger and Benue Rivers. Often, the flooding moves through towns and villages like Ibaji as it enters the Altantic Ocean. Most recently, Kogi State in particular experienced its worst flooding in more than 25 years which has lead to massive food insecurity, lack of source of income and homelessness have forced women and girls to practice negative coping strategies, including survival sex, exploitation, and forced and early marriage. Men have also become disempowered and are unable to meet social expectations, thereby increasing the risk to women and girls of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). This project will seek to improve food security and to reduce negative coping strategies in Idah and Ibaji LGAs in Kogi State. The project will target five (5) communities in Ibaji and Idah LGAs. The project will target 1260HHs approx. 7,560 IDPs and Host community members (6 people in each household) 60% female, 35% male and 5% PWD. The beneficiaries of cash will be participating in the awareness raising sessions on protection and climate change in order to meet up and fulfill the set objective of this project, which is to improve food security and livelihood status of vulnerable households through environmentally sensitive cash transfer programming and income generating activities.
